contract_plain_english: For a fixed probability space (Ω, Σ, P) and a fixed positive real exponent p, with p = ∞ included by a separate extension, the source defines Lp(Ω, Σ, P) to be the collection of real random variables X on Ω whose Lp quantity is finite. For finite p this quantity is (E|X|^p)^(1/p), and at ∞ it is ess sup |X| [PDF pages 1–2, printed pages 5–6; Section 1.1 formulas and displayed set definition]. The source includes 0 < p < 1 in this collection while warning that the quantity is not then a norm; for 1 ≤ p ≤ ∞ it calls Lp a Banach space [PDF page 2, printed page 6; paragraph after the definition]. The printed text relies on the inherited notion of random variable and does not explicitly formulate measurability, almost-sure equality, equivalence classes, or a quotient. Thus those standard measure-theoretic implementation choices must not be misreported as words present in the source [PDF page 1, printed page 5, introductory context and footnote 1; PDF page 2, printed page 6, complete definition and following paragraph].
